laws.rule: In Sardinia it is an offence to take away, keep or sell even small amounts of sand, pebbles, stones or shells from the coast or the sea without a permit from the authorities. The fine is EUR 500 to EUR 3,000 (about A$795 to A$4,767 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293), and the material is seized. Customs officers check luggage at Sardinian ports and airports and return seized material to the beaches.

sites.name: Su Nuraxi di Barumini
sites.era: Nuragic, Bronze Age to Iron Age
sites.what: Nuragic tower complex and village in south-central Sardinia (UNESCO World Heritage).

access.opening: Open every day of the year. Guided visit compulsory, leaving every 30 minutes, about an hour.
access.tickets: Single ticket EUR 16 (about AUD 25, RBA rate 30 October 2026) covering Su Nuraxi, Casa Zapata and the Giovanni Lilliu centre; EUR 8 if rain limits the visit to the outside (2026 price list, search snapshot).
access.permits: Groups and agencies must book by email.
access.closures: The area may be closed in bad weather for safety. No animals except guide dogs, which need a booking.

lore.text: Popular theories claim the nuraghe builders were the Shardana of the ancient 'Sea Peoples', or even survivors of Atlantis.
lore.label: popular lore, not an official source
